```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# VERSION MARKER
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.align = "center")
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggtext)
library(grid)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

condition_colors <- c("Good" = "#009E73", "Fair" = "#F0E442", "Poor" = "#D55E00", "Missing" = "#9E9E9E")
condition_levels <- c("Good", "Fair", "Poor", "Missing")
```

```{r load-data}
# Load the master dashboard file and isolate this park's records
raw <- read_excel(params$data_file, sheet = "Sheet 1")
park_data <- raw %>% filter(Park == params$park_code)

# Select which year to report on
available_years <- sort(unique(park_data$Sample_Year))

if (identical(params$sample_year, "latest")) {
  current_year <- max(available_years, na.rm = TRUE)
} else {
  requested_year <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(params$sample_year))
  if (is.na(requested_year) || !(requested_year %in% available_years)) {
    stop(paste0(
      "params$sample_year = '", params$sample_year, "' is not available for park '",
      params$park_code, "'. Available years: ", paste(available_years, collapse = ", ")
    ))
  }
  current_year <- requested_year
}

prior_years  <- sort(unique(park_data$Sample_Year[park_data$Sample_Year < current_year]), decreasing = TRUE)
prior_year   <- if (length(prior_years) > 0) prior_years[1] else NA

current_data <- park_data %>% filter(Sample_Year == current_year)
prior_data   <- if (!is.na(prior_year)) park_data %>% filter(Sample_Year == prior_year) else NULL

# Stratum names, for parks with more than one stratum
stratum_names <- list(
  CACO = c(`1` = "Pleasant Bay", `2` = "Nauset Harbor", `3` = "Salt Ponds"),
  COLO = c(`1` = "Thoroughfare", `2` = "Tidal Creeks")
)

n_strata_park    <- length(unique(current_data$Stratum))
is_multi_stratum <- n_strata_park > 1
this_stratum_ids <- sort(unique(current_data$Stratum))
this_stratum_names <- if (is_multi_stratum) stratum_names[[params$park_code]] else NULL

# Aggregation logic
pct_by_condition <- function(data, cond_col) {
  data %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[cond_col]]), .data[[cond_col]] != "") %>%
    group_by(Condition = .data[[cond_col]]) %>%
    summarise(Percent = sum(Percent_Tot, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(Percent = pmin(pmax(round(Percent, 6), 0), 100)) %>%
    mutate(Condition = ifelse(Condition == "", "Missing", Condition)) %>%
    complete(Condition = condition_levels, fill = list(Percent = 0)) %>%
    mutate(Condition = factor(Condition, levels = condition_levels)) %>%
    filter(!(Condition == "Missing" & Percent == 0))
}

pct_within_stratum <- function(data, stratum_id, cond_col) {
  data %>%
    filter(Stratum == stratum_id, !is.na(.data[[cond_col]]), .data[[cond_col]] != "") %>%
    group_by(Condition = .data[[cond_col]]) %>%
    summarise(Percent = sum(Percent_tot_Strat, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(Percent = pmin(pmax(round(Percent, 6), 0), 100)) %>%
    mutate(Condition = ifelse(Condition == "", "Missing", Condition)) %>%
    complete(Condition = condition_levels, fill = list(Percent = 0)) %>%
    mutate(Condition = factor(Condition, levels = condition_levels)) %>%
    filter(!(Condition == "Missing" & Percent == 0))
}

do_df   <- pct_by_condition(current_data, "Condition_DO")
chla_df <- pct_by_condition(current_data, "Condition_CHLA")
kd_df   <- pct_by_condition(current_data, "Condition_Kd")

build_trend_df <- function(data, cond_col, stratum_id = NULL) {
  yrs <- sort(unique(data$Sample_Year))
  bind_rows(lapply(yrs, function(y) {
    yr_data <- data %>% filter(Sample_Year == y)
    result <- if (is.null(stratum_id)) {
      pct_by_condition(yr_data, cond_col)
    } else {
      pct_within_stratum(yr_data, stratum_id, cond_col)
    }
    result %>% mutate(Year = y)
  }))
}

build_trend_df_faceted <- function(data, cond_col, stratum_ids, stratum_label_map) {
  bind_rows(lapply(stratum_ids, function(sid) {
    build_trend_df(data, cond_col, stratum_id = sid) %>%
      mutate(StratumLabel = stratum_label_map[[as.character(sid)]])
  })) %>%
    mutate(StratumLabel = factor(StratumLabel, levels = unname(stratum_label_map[as.character(stratum_ids)])))
}

do_trend   <- build_trend_df(park_data, "Condition_DO")
chla_trend <- build_trend_df(park_data, "Condition_CHLA")
kd_trend   <- build_trend_df(park_data, "Condition_Kd")

if (is_multi_stratum) {
  do_trend_strata   <- build_trend_df_faceted(park_data, "Condition_DO",   this_stratum_ids, this_stratum_names)
  chla_trend_strata <- build_trend_df_faceted(park_data, "Condition_CHLA", this_stratum_ids, this_stratum_names)
  kd_trend_strata   <- build_trend_df_faceted(park_data, "Condition_Kd",   this_stratum_ids, this_stratum_names)
}

current_kd_val   <- sum(current_data$Weighted_Kd,   na.rm = TRUE)
current_do_val   <- sum(current_data$Weighted_DO,   na.rm = TRUE)
current_chla_val <- sum(current_data$Weighted_CHYA, na.rm = TRUE)

get_pct <- function(df, cond) {
  val <- df$Percent[df$Condition == cond]
  if (length(val) == 0 || is.na(val)) return(0)
  round(val, 1)
}

majority_condition <- function(df) {
  scored <- df %>% filter(Condition %in% c("Good", "Fair", "Poor"))
  if (nrow(scored) == 0 || all(scored$Percent == 0)) return(NA_character_)
  as.character(scored$Condition[which.max(scored$Percent)])
}

do_majority   <- majority_condition(do_df)
chla_majority <- majority_condition(chla_df)
kd_majority   <- majority_condition(kd_df)

if (!is.null(prior_data)) {
  do_prior_df   <- pct_by_condition(prior_data, "Condition_DO")
  chla_prior_df <- pct_by_condition(prior_data, "Condition_CHLA")
  kd_prior_df   <- pct_by_condition(prior_data, "Condition_Kd")
}

concern_indicators <- c(
  if (!is.na(do_majority)   && do_majority   != "Good") "bottom water dissolved oxygen",
  if (!is.na(chla_majority) && chla_majority != "Good") "surface water chlorophyll-<em>a</em>",
  if (!is.na(kd_majority)   && kd_majority   != "Good") "water column light attenuation"
)

# Park-specific Site Context paragraphs, keyed by park_code.
site_context_text <- list(
  FIIS = "Fire Island National Seashore (FIIS) is a 19,580-acre park unit on the South Shore of Long Island, New York (Fig. 1). Approximately 46% of this area is submerged estuarine land in Great South Bay and Moriches Bay. Although FIIS owns only a minority portion of the submerged estuarine land in these bays, the area in park ownership is extensive.",
  CACO = "Cape Cod is a large glacial moraine peninsula that extends 96.5 km into the Atlantic Ocean from the coast of Massachusetts. Cape Cod National Seashore (CACO) is located on the outer portion of Cape Cod (Fig. 1). Almost all the estuarine habitat at CACO is associated with two large coastal lagoon systems, Pleasant Bay (PB) and Nauset Harbor/Marsh (NH). Due to restricted flushing with the ocean and residential development pressures outside the seashore boundary, the National Park Service (NPS) interest in estuarine condition extends throughout these coastal embayments, not just in the areas within the seashore boundary. Pleasant Bay and Nauset Harbor are each fringed by small, deep, glacially-formed kettle-hole salt ponds that flush with seawater from the lagoons. Because deep water replacement may be restricted through density stratification, and the presence of shallow sills at their mouths, these estuarine kettle-holes are particularly susceptible to over-enrichment.",
  GATE = "Gateway National Recreation Area (GATE) consists of 26,645 acres of coastal uplands, freshwater ponds, marshes, bays, beaches, and mudflats. Established in 1972, it is divided into three geographically separate units: Jamaica Bay, Staten Island, and Sandy Hook. The Jamaica Bay Unit (GATE-JBU) encompasses almost all of the island uplands and wetlands within Jamaica Bay (Fig. 1). Thus, estuarine resources of GATE are fully contained within Jamaica Bay. The target population for estuarine monitoring includes 100% of these resources, approximately 11,404 acres, plus an additional 3,106 acres within Jamaica Bay but outside the park boundary.",
  COLO = "Colonial National Historical Park (COLO) consists of two significant land holdings, the Yorktown and Jamestown Units (Fig. 1). These are connected by a narrow traffic corridor, the Colonial Parkway. COLO estuarine sampling area is divided into two strata. The first, the Tidal Creeks stratum, includes all estuarine resources falling inside park boundaries. This includes small tidal creeks that drain off park wetlands, the small regions of park ownership where the Colonial Parkway overpasses tidal creeks, and a few additional areas where the park boundary does not precisely coincide with a tidal creek shoreline. The second, Jamestown Island/Thoroughfare stratum, includes non-NPS estuarine resources in Sandy Bay, Back River and The Thoroughfare. The sample area is defined to exclude the non-NPS estuarine resources associated with the James River or York River. These are major systems outside COLO boundaries and attempting to monitor them in any meaningful fashion would severely dilute NPS efforts within the park and at Jamestown. Between both strata, approximately 724 acres of estuary are monitored, including 100% of the estuarine resources that fall within the park boundary.",
  GEWA = "George Washington Birthplace National Monument (GEWA) is located along the tidal reaches of the Potomac River in Westmoreland County, Virginia (Fig. 1). The Potomac shoreline delineates the northern boundary of the monument, where three small sub-basins drain into the Potomac. The largest and most significant estuarine resource is Popes Creek, which has restricted flushing with the Potomac and is closely linked to GEWA resources. The monitoring area covers all tidal portions of Popes Creek, which includes approximately 340 acres of estuary outside and 12 acres inside the park.",
  ASIS = "Assateague Island National Seashore (ASIS) is a 60km long barrier island off the eastern coast of the Delmarva Peninsula, extending into the Atlantic Ocean (Fig. 1). The northern two-thirds of the island are in Maryland, while the southern third is in Virginia. ASIS is one of two NER coastal parks with a highly developed water-quality monitoring program, through a joint effort among many federal and state partners. The park boundary encircles the NPS holdings, Chincoteague National Wildlife Refuge (U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service), and Assateague State Park (State, MD). Further, Sinepuxent Bay and the MD portion of Chincoteague Bay are managed under the Maryland Coastal Bays Program as a National Estuary Program estuary. Therefore, the park has monitoring interests throughout the coastal bay and is not confined in its interests to the area within the park boundary. Approximately 92,217 acres of estuary are monitored for this protocol. About 16,969 acres of that area fall inside park boundaries, representing 100% of NPS estuarine resources within ASIS."
)

# Park-specific Sampling Design paragraphs, keyed by park code.
sampling_design_text <- list(
  FIIS = "Water quality is assessed at approximately 30 stations distributed throughout the estuary using a randomized, spatially balanced design, maximizing the likelihood that results are representative of the entire system. This total includes 6 fixed trend stations, visited repeatedly over time to track long-term change. While trend stations were sampled multiple times across each four-week index period, only one representative sampling event per trend station is included in the system-wide figures presented here, consistent with treatment of the 24 random spatial stations.
  
Sampling occurred during a four-week summer index period (July–August), timed to coincide with the warm-season conditions when the effects of nutrient enrichment, including low dissolved oxygen, elevated chlorophyll-<em>a</em>, and reduced water clarity, are typically most pronounced. NCBN has been monitoring water quality at FIIS biennially since 2003.

Because each sampling location statistically represents a proportional share of the surrounding estuary, results can be scaled up to describe conditions across the full monitored area. The area-weighted mean (Figs. 3, 5, 7) reflects this approach, calculating an average condition value weighted by the amount of estuary each station represents. Similarly, the percent of total estuarine area in each condition category (Figs. 2, 4, 6) reflects the proportion of the estuary's surface area represented by stations falling into good, fair, or poor condition.",

The Salt Ponds stratum does not include trend stations. While trend stations were sampled multiple times across each four-week index period, only one representative sampling event per trend station is included in the figures presented here, consistent with treatment of the spatial stations.

# Helper: safely pull a commentary entry, returning NULL (nothing printed) if the park or
# stratum key doesn't exist yet, rather than erroring.
get_commentary <- function(commentary_list, park_code, key) {
  park_entry <- commentary_list[[park_code]]
  if (is.null(park_entry)) return(NULL)
  park_entry[[key]]
}
```

```{r indicator-sentence-helpers}
join_list_with_and <- function(parts) {
  n <- length(parts)
  if (n == 0) return("")
  if (n == 1) return(parts[1])
  if (n == 2) return(paste0(parts[1], " and ", parts[2]))
  paste0(paste(parts[1:(n-1)], collapse = ", "), ", and ", parts[n])
}

# Builds a "good/fair/poor" sentence for DO. Conditions are always listed in a fixed
# Good/Fair/Poor/Missing order (NOT reordered by percentage size) -- the majority condition is
# bolded wherever it falls in that fixed order. Optional fig_ref appends a "(Fig. N)" citation
# before the closing period. Optional manual_note is appended as a separate sentence after.
build_do_sentence <- function(df, area_label, fig_ref = NULL, manual_note = NULL) {
  majority <- majority_condition(df)
  parts <- c()
  for (c in c("Good", "Fair", "Poor", "Missing")) {
    p <- get_pct(df, c)
    if (p > 0) {
      clause <- paste0(tolower(c), " within ", p, "%")
      if (!is.na(majority) && c == majority) clause <- paste0("**", clause, "**")
      parts <- c(parts, clause)
    }
  }

  sentence <- join_list_with_and(parts)
  fig_clause <- if (!is.null(fig_ref)) paste0(" (", fig_ref, ")") else ""
  sentence <- paste0(sentence, " ", area_label, fig_clause, ".")
  if (!is.null(manual_note)) sentence <- paste0(sentence, " ", manual_note)
  sentence
}

# Builds a majority-led sentence for CHLA/Kd. Conditions are always listed in a fixed
# Good/Fair/Poor/Missing order (NOT reordered by percentage size) -- the majority condition is
# still bolded wherever it falls in that fixed order. Optional fig_ref appends a "(Fig. N)"
# citation. Optional manual_note is appended after.
build_majority_sentence <- function(df, area_label, fig_ref = NULL, manual_note = NULL) {
  majority <- majority_condition(df)
  if (is.na(majority)) return("No condition data are available for this area.")

  parts <- c()
  for (c in c("Good", "Fair", "Poor", "Missing")) {
    p <- get_pct(df, c)
    if (p > 0) {
      clause <- paste0(tolower(c), " within ", p, "%")
      if (c == majority) clause <- paste0("**", clause, "**")
      parts <- c(parts, clause)
    }
  }

  fig_clause <- if (!is.null(fig_ref)) paste0(" (", fig_ref, ")") else ""
  sentence <- paste0(join_list_with_and(parts), " ", area_label, fig_clause, ".")
  if (!is.null(manual_note)) sentence <- paste0(sentence, " ", manual_note)
  sentence
}
```

```{r plot-functions}
plot_trend <- function(trend_df, current_year, title, legend_labels) {
  years_sorted <- sort(unique(trend_df$Year), decreasing = TRUE)
  axis_order   <- rev(years_sorted)
  current_pos  <- which(axis_order == current_year)

  trend_df <- trend_df %>%
    mutate(Percent    = pmin(pmax(round(Percent, 2), 0), 100),
           Condition  = factor(Condition, levels = condition_levels),
           YearFactor = factor(Year, levels = axis_order),
           is_current = Year == current_year)

  axis_label_sizes  <- ifelse(axis_order == current_year, 12, 9)
  axis_label_colors <- ifelse(axis_order == current_year, "black", "gray40")

  ggplot(trend_df, aes(x = Percent, y = YearFactor, fill = Condition)) +
    geom_col(aes(alpha = is_current), position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE), width = 0.72,
             color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = -2, xmax = 102,
             ymin = current_pos - 0.46, ymax = current_pos + 0.46,
             fill = NA, color = "#212121", linewidth = 1) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = condition_colors, name = NULL, drop = FALSE, labels = legend_labels) +
    scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 1, `FALSE` = 0.4), guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"), breaks = seq(0, 100, 25),
                        position = "top", expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05)), limits = c(0, 100),
                        oob = scales::squish) +
    labs(title = title, x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "gray85"),
      axis.text.y  = element_text(size = axis_label_sizes, color = axis_label_colors, face = "bold"),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
      plot.title = ggtext::element_markdown(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 12, margin = margin(b = 8)),
      plot.margin = margin(t = 8, r = 12, b = 5.5, l = 5.5)
    )
}

plot_trend_faceted <- function(trend_df, current_year, title, legend_labels) {
  years_sorted <- sort(unique(trend_df$Year), decreasing = TRUE)
  axis_order   <- rev(years_sorted)
  current_pos  <- which(axis_order == current_year)

  trend_df <- trend_df %>%
    mutate(Percent    = pmin(pmax(round(Percent, 2), 0), 100),
           Condition  = factor(Condition, levels = condition_levels),
           YearFactor = factor(Year, levels = axis_order),
           is_current = Year == current_year)

  axis_label_sizes  <- ifelse(axis_order == current_year, 10, 7.5)
  axis_label_colors <- ifelse(axis_order == current_year, "black", "gray40")

  box_df <- data.frame(StratumLabel = unique(trend_df$StratumLabel))

  ggplot(trend_df, aes(x = Percent, y = YearFactor, fill = Condition)) +
    geom_col(aes(alpha = is_current), position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE), width = 0.72,
             color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_rect(data = box_df, inherit.aes = FALSE,
              aes(xmin = -2, xmax = 102, ymin = current_pos - 0.46, ymax = current_pos + 0.46),
              fill = NA, color = "#212121", linewidth = 0.9) +
    facet_wrap(~ StratumLabel, nrow = 1, strip.position = "bottom") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = condition_colors, name = NULL, drop = FALSE, labels = legend_labels) +
    scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 1, `FALSE` = 0.4), guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"), breaks = seq(0, 100, 25),
                        position = "top", expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.06)), limits = c(0, 100),
                        oob = scales::squish) +
    labs(title = title, x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "gray85"),
      panel.spacing = unit(1.6, "lines"),
      axis.text.y  = element_text(size = axis_label_sizes, color = axis_label_colors, face = "bold"),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      strip.placement = "outside",
      strip.text   = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9.5, margin = margin(t = 8)),
      strip.background = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.text = element_text(size = 7.5),
      plot.title = ggtext::element_markdown(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 11, margin = margin(b = 6)),
      plot.margin = margin(t = 8, r = 12, b = 5.5, l = 5.5)
    )
}

make_gauge <- function(value, bands, max_value, unit, title) {
  to_angle <- function(v) 180 - 180 * (v / max_value)

  arc_points <- function(a_start, a_end, r, n = 60) {
    angs <- seq(a_start, a_end, length.out = n) * pi / 180
    data.frame(x = r * cos(angs), y = r * sin(angs))
  }

  r_out <- 1; r_in <- 0.62

  band_polys <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(bands)), function(i) {
    a1 <- to_angle(bands$from[i]); a2 <- to_angle(bands$to[i])
    poly <- rbind(arc_points(a1, a2, r_out), arc_points(a2, a1, r_in))
    poly$group <- bands$label[i]
    poly$fill  <- bands$color[i]
    poly
  }))

  val_clamped  <- max(0, min(value, max_value))
  needle_angle <- to_angle(val_clamped) * pi / 180
  needle_df <- data.frame(x = c(0, 0.5 * cos(needle_angle)),
                           y = c(0, 0.5 * sin(needle_angle)))

  ticks <- sort(unique(c(0, bands$from, bands$to)))
  ticks <- ticks[ticks != max(ticks)]  # VERIFIED v61: explicitly drop whichever value is highest,
  # since the Poor band's own upper bound always equals max_value in every gauge (12 for DO, 30 for
  # CHLA, 2.5 for Kd) -- removing max_value alone wasn't enough, since it re-entered via bands$to
  tick_df <- data.frame(val = ticks, ang = to_angle(ticks) * pi / 180)
  tick_df$xr <- 1.16 * cos(tick_df$ang)
  tick_df$yr <- 1.16 * sin(tick_df$ang)
  tick_df$lab <- ifelse(tick_df$val == round(tick_df$val), as.character(tick_df$val), sprintf("%.2f", tick_df$val))

  bands$mid     <- (bands$from + bands$to) / 2
  bands$ang_mid <- to_angle(bands$mid) * pi / 180
  bands$xl <- 0.81 * cos(bands$ang_mid)
  bands$yl <- 0.81 * sin(bands$ang_mid)

  ggplot() +
    geom_polygon(data = band_polys, aes(x = x, y = y, group = group, fill = fill)) +
    scale_fill_identity() +
    geom_segment(data = needle_df[1, ],
                 aes(x = x, y = y, xend = needle_df$x[2], yend = needle_df$y[2]),
                 linewidth = 1.7, color = "#212121", lineend = "round") +
    geom_point(aes(x = 0, y = 0), size = 5, color = "#212121") +
    geom_text(data = tick_df, aes(x = xr, y = yr, label = lab), size = 4.3, color = "gray30") +  # VERIFIED v60: larger tick labels
    geom_text(data = bands, aes(x = xl, y = yl, label = label), size = 3.7, fontface = "bold", color = "#1a1a1a") +
    annotate("text", x = 0, y = -0.32, label = paste0(round(value, 2), " ", unit),
             size = 5.6, fontface = "bold", color = "#212121") +
    ggtext::geom_richtext(aes(x = 0, y = 1.34, label = title), size = 4.5, fontface = "bold",
                          fill = NA, label.color = NA) +
    coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1.35, 1.35), ylim = c(-0.5, 1.5)) +
    theme_void()
}
```

## Shallow Dive

::: quick-dive-box
Many of our coastal parks are home to dynamic estuaries, where saltwater meets freshwater. These waters also experience the detrimental effects of estuarine nutrient enrichment, largely from human activities, that impact water quality. Nutrient over-enrichment is the excessive accumulation of nutrients, such as nitrogen and phosphorus, which leads to over-growth of algae. The Northeast Coastal and Barrier Network (NCBN) parks depend on high-quality aquatic resources to sustain complex estuarine and near-shore ecosystems. Read more about our water quality monitoring program by [visiting our website](https://home.nps.gov/im/ncbn/estuarine-water-quality.htm) and learn more about [estuarine nutrient enrichment through our infographic](https://www.nps.gov/articles/000/what-we-mean-when-we-talk-about-estuarine-nutrient-enrichment.htm) series.
:::

`r site_context_text[[params$park_code]]`

The threat of nutrient enrichment is a primary management concern. Water quality monitoring follows Northeast Coastal and Barrier Network's *Protocol for Monitoring Estuarine Nutrient Enrichment* (Kopp and Neckles, 2009). The protocol's primary goal is to assess how estuarine natural resources are affected by changing nutrient inputs by determining the status and trends of response indicators within the monitored estuarine areas of each park.

Presented here are condition status summaries of three key response indicators:

1.  Bottom water dissolved oxygen
2.  Surface water chlorophyll-*a*
3.  Water column light attenuation (K<sub>d</sub>)

```{r strata-note, results='asis'}
if (is_multi_stratum) {
  strat_list_text <- paste(this_stratum_names[as.character(this_stratum_ids)], collapse = ", ")
  cat(paste0("The condition of these indicators is presented for the entire monitored area, providing a system-wide condition across all strata, and for each individual stratum: ", strat_list_text, "."))
}
```

Threshold values are used to determine "good," "fair," and "poor" condition categories (Table 2), which are consistent with those used by the US Environmental Protection Agency (USEPA) for national coastal condition reporting (USEPA 2001b, 2004) and thresholds used by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Association for the National Estuarine Eutrophication Assessment (Bricker et al. 1999).

Light attenuation through the water column, or water clarity, is expressed as K<sub>d</sub> (m<sup>-1</sup>) coefficient. Cutoff values (Table 2) for the three condition categories of K<sub>d</sub> have been calculated from the USEPA criteria for turbidity, using the thresholds for areas with significant submerged aquatic vegetation (SAV).

```{r table1-thresholds}
thresholds_df <- data.frame(
  Measure = c("Dissolved oxygen", "Chlorophyll-<em>a</em>", "Light attenuation (K<sub>d</sub>)"),
  Good = c("> 5 mg/L", "< 5 \u00b5g/L", "< 0.92 m<sup>-1</sup>"),
  Fair = c("2\u20135 mg/L", "5\u201320 \u00b5g/L", "0.92\u20131.61 m<sup>-1</sup>"),
  Poor = c("< 2 mg/L", "> 20 \u00b5g/L", "> 1.61 m<sup>-1</sup>")
)

kable(thresholds_df, format = "html", caption = "Table 2: Threshold values associated with each measured nutrient enrichment condition category.", align = "lccc", escape = FALSE) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("striped", "bordered")) %>%
  column_spec(2, background = "#E6F7F1") %>%
  column_spec(3, background = "#FDFBE0") %>%
  column_spec(4, background = "#FBE5DC")
```

## Bottom Water Dissolved Oxygen

:::::: indicator-flex
::: indicator-text
Bottom water dissolved oxygen (DO) concentration is an indirect indicator of nutrient load and direct indicator of estuarine water chemistry and organism health.

In estuaries, microbial decomposers consume oxygen when they break down organic matter on and within the sediment. When sediment organic matter increases due to nutrient over-enrichment, it can cause an overgrowth of nuisance algae.

The excess of organic matter increases microbial breakdown and can lower DO concentrations in bottom water. It can also lead to increased extent and duration of bottom water anoxia and toxic sulfide concentrations. Low levels of dissolved oxygen and associated nutrient enrichment can, ultimately, impact fauna diversity and abundance and shift species dominance.

```{r do-section, results='asis'}
if (is_multi_stratum) cat("#### All Strata\n\n")

cat(paste0("During the ", current_year, " summer index period, ", params$park_code,
           " system-wide average bottom water dissolved oxygen concentrations were ",
           build_do_sentence(do_df, "of the total sampled estuarine area", fig_ref = "Fig. 2",
                              manual_note = get_commentary(do_commentary, params$park_code, "park_wide")),
           " The system-wide weighted mean concentration was **", round(current_do_val, 2), " mg/L** (Fig. 3).\n\n"))

if (is_multi_stratum) {
  for (sid in this_stratum_ids) {
    sname <- this_stratum_names[[as.character(sid)]]
    strat_do_df <- pct_within_stratum(current_data, sid, "Condition_DO")
    cat(paste0("#### ", sname, "\n\n"))
    cat(paste0("Average bottom water DO concentration was ",
               build_do_sentence(strat_do_df, paste0("of the ", sname, " stratum"), fig_ref = "Fig. 2",
                                  manual_note = get_commentary(do_commentary, params$park_code, sname)), "\n\n"))
  }
}
```

## Surface Water Chlorophyll-*a*

:::::: indicator-flex
::: indicator-text
Nutrient enrichment often stimulates phytoplankton production, leading to population growth. Phytoplankton growth is often nutrient-limited. Trends of increasing phytoplankton biomass can suggest increasing nutrient load. Surface water chlorophyll-<em>a</em> concentration is an indicator of phytoplankton population growth, nutrient enrichment, and overall water quality.

```{r chla-section, results='asis'}
if (is_multi_stratum) cat("#### All Strata\n\n")

cat(paste0("During the ", current_year, " summer index period, ", params$park_code,
           " system-wide average surface water chlorophyll-<em>a</em> concentration was ",
           build_majority_sentence(chla_df, "of the sampled estuarine area", fig_ref = "Fig. 4",
                                    manual_note = get_commentary(chla_commentary, params$park_code, "park_wide")),
           " The system-wide weighted mean concentration was **", round(current_chla_val, 2), " \u00b5g/L** (Fig. 5).\n\n"))

if (is_multi_stratum) {
  for (sid in this_stratum_ids) {
    sname <- this_stratum_names[[as.character(sid)]]
    strat_chla_df <- pct_within_stratum(current_data, sid, "Condition_CHLA")
    cat(paste0("#### ", sname, "\n\n"))
    cat(paste0("Average surface water chlorophyll-<em>a</em> concentration was ",
               build_majority_sentence(strat_chla_df, paste0("of the ", sname, " stratum"), fig_ref = "Fig. 4",
                                        manual_note = get_commentary(chla_commentary, params$park_code, sname)), "\n\n"))
  }
}
```

## Water Column Light Attenuation

:::::: indicator-flex
::: indicator-text
Light attenuation through the water column, represented here by coefficient K<sub>d</sub>, is dependent on concentrations of phytoplankton, which can correlate with nutrient enrichment, and suspended inorganic and dissolved organic matter.

**High** **K**<sub>**d**</sub>**:** The water is more turbid, muddy, or full of algae. Light attenuates (fades) near the surface, leaving deeper areas dark.

**Low K**<sub>**d**</sub>**:** The water is clearer. Light can penetrate deeper into the water column.

Submerged aquatic vegetation (SAV) provides important ecosystem services, and their productivity and distribution depend on light. Regardless of current SAV presence, NCBN continues to monitor this critical SAV parameter, as it provides information relevant to the overall estuarine eutrophication status.

```{r kd-section, results='asis'}
if (is_multi_stratum) cat("#### All Strata\n\n")

cat(paste0("During the ", current_year, " summer index period, ", params$park_code,
           " system-wide average water column light attenuation (K<sub>d</sub>) was ",
           build_majority_sentence(kd_df, "of the sampled estuarine area", fig_ref = "Fig. 6",
                                    manual_note = get_commentary(kd_commentary, params$park_code, "park_wide")),
           " The system-wide weighted mean K<sub>d</sub> was **", round(current_kd_val, 2), " m<sup>-1</sup>** (Fig. 7).\n\n"))

if (is_multi_stratum) {
  for (sid in this_stratum_ids) {
    sname <- this_stratum_names[[as.character(sid)]]
    strat_kd_df <- pct_within_stratum(current_data, sid, "Condition_Kd")
    cat(paste0("#### ", sname, "\n\n"))
    cat(paste0("Average water column light attenuation was ",
               build_majority_sentence(strat_kd_df, paste0("of the ", sname, " stratum"), fig_ref = "Fig. 6",
                                        manual_note = get_commentary(kd_commentary, params$park_code, sname)), "\n\n"))
  }
}
```

## Conclusion

```{r conclusion-text, results='asis'}
concl <- conclusion_commentary[[params$park_code]]

if (!is.null(concl$body)) {
  cat(" ", concl$body)
}

if (!is.null(concl$closing)) {
  cat('\n\n<div class="conclusion-box">\n\n')
  cat("**", concl$closing, "**", sep = "")
  cat('\n\n</div>\n')
}
```

The continued monitoring of estuarine nutrient enrichment vital signs will be essential for managers to make informed decisions, develop effective mitigation measures, reduce management costs, and provide a means of measuring progress towards goals.

These briefs are intended to provide a snapshot of the most recent water quality monitoring data available from NCBN. Continued monitoring will help clarify whether these observed changes in condition represent isolated index-period variation or the start of a longer-term pattern. For in-depth trend analysis of this data, [read NCBN's Water Quality Trend Reports.](https://irma.nps.gov/DataStore/Collection/Profile/10039)
